flawed_step: Step 1—the standard augmentation argument that every legal augmentation preserves feasibility and strictly increases the flow value—is justified. Step 2, inferring finite termination from this increase and the finite capacity bound, is not justified for arbitrary real capacities: the positive bottlenecks can approach zero, so a bounded strictly increasing sequence of flow values can contain infinitely many augmentations.
counterexample: Let r=(sqrt(5)-1)/2, so 0<r<1 and 1-r=r^2. Use vertices s,t,a1,b1,a2,b2,a3,b3. The three special directed edges are e1=a1->b1 of capacity 1, e2=a2->b2 of capacity r, and e3=a3->b3 of capacity r. Give capacity 10 to each of the following edges: s->a1, s->a2, b1->t, b2->t, s->b1, a1->b2, a2->a3, b3->t, s->b3, a3->b1, a1->a2, s->b2, a2->b3, a3->a1. No other edges exist. Starting with zero flow, first augment along s->a1->b1->t by 1, then along s->a2->b2->t by r. Thus (f(e1),f(e2),f(e3))=(1,r,0). Now repeat forever the following three residual paths, where a traversal bi->ai is the reverse residual arc of ei: P0=s->b1->a1->b2->a2->a3->b3->t; P1=s->b3->a3->b1->a1->a2->b2->t; P2=s->b2->a2->b3->a3->a1->b1->t. Before P0 in repetition m>=0, the special-edge flows are (r^(3m),r^(3m+1),0). Its bottleneck is r^(3m+1), after which the flows are (r^(3m+2),0,r^(3m+1)). P1 then has bottleneck r^(3m+2) and leaves (0,r^(3m+2),r^(3m+3)). P2 has bottleneck r^(3m+3) and leaves (r^(3m+3),r^(3m+4),0), establishing the invariant for repetition m+1. These identities use r^k-r^(k+1)=r^(k+2). Every bottleneck is positive, so every listed path remains a legal augmenting path. The total amount ever sent, including initialization, is 1+r+sum_{n>=1}r^n=2(1+r)<10; hence every capacity-10 edge always has residual capacity greater than any special-edge bottleneck and never obstructs the schedule. The schedule therefore performs infinitely many legal augmentations, contradicting the claimed termination for every path choice.
assessment_summary: The claim is false. The usual finite-termination proof needs a discrete lower bound on positive augmentation amounts, available for integral or suitably scaled rational capacities but absent for arbitrary real capacities. The explicit golden-ratio network above admits bottlenecks r,r^2,r^3,... and therefore an infinite legal Ford-Fulkerson schedule.
